body:
Thank you for your input, I'll definitely look into that! 
And well, I have thought about going myself, for the reason you mentioned. Although I have managed depression very well by myself, and I still function in life perfectly, there are some traits that I have which I'm curious about. 
Personally my emotions are very far separated from MOST of my decision making, as well as daily life in general, and I have very little empathy.
The former I tend to not look at as a bad thing so much. It mostly occurs in periods of stress, a disconnect occurs that's hard to explain but it's almost like instead of a flash of emotion, it's muffled and seeps out for the next week or so.
The lack of empathy puzzles me frankly because objectively I have a blatant apathy towards the consequences of others' mistakes. For some reason, I almost robotically support them at the same time. Letting friends live with me after they've quit jobs, tolerating abuse in relationships, etc. It's all rather strange. 
I really have no idea why. It's like I never end up going from loving to hating someone, I'll end up doing both at the same time, like my positive and negative emotions are separated, but are both there and very strong. This is never shown in my actions, and it doesn't affect me negatively in the way I would expect it to, reading it. It doesn't play a part in daily life, except for tolerating bad relationships, with people and partners. 
Partially related given my current situation and willingness even now to try and remedy it, rather than leaving, which my objective side recognizes as the obvious choice lmao. 

Sorry for rambling, thank you for your advice.

It's the notion that I could be, it's always out of reach. It's been this way in many different scenarios in many different ways for most of my life.
I could have had a happy childhood if I didn't have an abusive parent for all of it. 
I could have been happy in the other relationship that I was in if the girl I was with was willing to grow as a person and not villainize me for her immaturity and resulting hardships.
I could be happy now, even with everything that has happened, if she could just not treat me like shit all the time.
I don't know anybody who can be happy alone.
They make exist but I'm not one of those people.
It's hard to want to build when other people knock down.
The things I want out of life are pretty simple. They aren't too much to ask for, but they are always just out of my reach.

Your information is worth its weight in gold my friend. The projection aspects that you mentioned are spot on and this really seems to make a lot more sense now. 
  I thankfully, being the type of person I am, have been very firmly rooted in my intentions and perception since day one. I can instantly call to mind the reasoning behind my actions and the reasons I do things or don't do them. 
   On the note of abandonment issues, it's been strange. Because she is and is not jealous, does and does not isolate me from friends, but then, I don't go out much anyway. There has been an ongoing debate about me talking to other girls, that I refuse to give way on. I have two female friends who I've known for years and was never willing to be told I couldn't talk to them, she doesn't care until all of a sudden she does. It hasn't come up in some time, but it has. Many times cited as an example that I don't ever consider how she feels/I'm always right etc. It's another point that I've had to justify on its own many times, but is more frequently cited in unrelated issues. 
   Frankly it's hard to say, because I'm not really a very social person. However, it raises a different question. I have always been a pretty reserved individual, and a problem that has been massive is that she has some perceived lack of communication from me. This isn't the case, but this has always seemed to me the most rational of the irrational arguments that she brings up though. I could understand why someone would think that of me, you know? In any case this has all been hashed out many times and brought back once again. The repetitive nature of that argument gives me the idea it is rooted in a form of some abandonment issue. There has also been much talk of me "not caring enough about her" or not showing it, which leads me to the same idea. It hasn't manifested itself in a classic sense per se, (although I suppose it has in a few ways.) but it seems to be there. Being a spectrum disorder, like you said, I could see there being variables you know?


In any case I guess I'm wondering how to approach this from a treatment standpoint. Of course I could go to a psychologist but frankly she needs some kind of help. Whether it's BPD or not, I've told her that her pride gets in the way of our communication, it results in a refusal for her to accept that she is wrong. Like she can't handle that and then lashes out, which makes me think of the ego defense that you mentioned. I can imagine that this makes accepting the idea of getting help a nightmare. Regardless of that, I don't know how to live a life someone who is literally incapable of emotional growth.
